title: Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) Defense Specialist (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O
raw_text:
2. MOS 5711, Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) Defense
Specialist (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O

    a. Summary. CBRN Defense Specialists operate within the unit combat
operations center to assist the staff in monitoring unit operations,
facilitating warning and reporting, and coordinating CBRN response
activities. CBRN Defense Specialists train personnel to employ individual
and organizational CBRN equipment and execute individual survival measures to
enable protective actions and sustain operations in a CBRN environment. CBRN
Defense Specialists collect, analyze and provide information relative to CBR
exposure status, location of contaminated areas and CBRN defense.
Additionally, CBRN Defense Specialists maintain and prepare CBRN defense
equipment for embarkation, deployment, and employment. This MOS is assigned
and voided only by the authority of the CMC (MM).

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Must possess a GT score of 110 or higher.

            (3) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

    c. Requirements. Complete the CBRN Specialist Basic Course (A16T3B4) at
the U.S. Marine Corps CBRN School, Ft Leonard Wood, MO.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks refer to
reference (ap), Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defense
Training and Readiness Manual. See also the 5711 MOS Road Map.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

        (1) Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists
and Crew Members, All Other 55-3019.

            (2) Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.



                                           3-325                        Enclosure (1)
 3135                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L
common_text: (CBRN) DEFENSE 1. Introduction. The Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear (CBRN) Defense Occupational Field includes planning and employing capabilities to enable the organization to accomplish its mission in a CBRN environment. This consists of forces capable of planning, detecting, identifying, warning and reporting, and mitigation of CBRN threats and hazards. CBRN Defense Specialists advise the staff on chemical and biological (CB) warfare agent characteristics, physiological symptoms and effects, treatment, detection and identification. They must coordinate and conduct training to ensure the organization is capable of mitigating the effects of nuclear explosions and detection of radiological hazards. CBRN Defense Specialist effectively instruct CBRN defense individual and unit survival measures and provide more in-depth training to their unit's CBRN defense team members. Additionally, CBRN Defense Specialists must be familiar with the proper employment, operation, maintenance, and supply procedures for all CBRN defense equipment and materials down to the battalion/squadron level.

(CBRN) DEFENSE 1. Introduction. The Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear (CBRN) Defense Occupational Field includes planning and employing capabilities to enable the organization to accomplish its mission in a CBRN environment. This consists of forces capable of planning, detecting, identifying, warning and reporting, and mitigation of CBRN threats and hazards. CBRN Defense Specialists advise the staff on chemical and biological (CB) warfare agent characteristics, physiological symptoms and effects, treatment, detection and identification. They must coordinate and conduct training to ensure the organization is capable of mitigating the effects of nuclear explosions and detection of radiological hazards. CBRN Defense Specialist effectively instruct CBRN defense individual and unit survival measures and provide more in-depth training to their unit's CBRN defense team members. Additionally, CBRN Defense Specialists must be familiar with the proper employment, operation, maintenance, and supply procedures for all CBRN defense equipment and materials down to the battalion/squadron level.

2. MOS 5711, Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) Defense Specialist (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O a. Summary. CBRN Defense Specialists operate within the unit combat operations center to assist the staff in monitoring unit operations, facilitating warning and reporting, and coordinating CBRN response activities. CBRN Defense Specialists train personnel to employ individual and organizational CBRN equipment and execute individual survival measures to enable protective actions and sustain operations in a CBRN environment. CBRN Defense Specialists collect, analyze and provide information relative to CBR exposure status, location of contaminated areas and CBRN defense. Additionally, CBRN Defense Specialists maintain and prepare CBRN defense equipment for embarkation, deployment, and employment. This MOS is assigned and voided only by the authority of the CMC (MM). b. Prerequisites (1) Must be a U.S. citizen. (2) Must possess a GT score of 110 or higher. (3) Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility. c. Requirements. Complete the CBRN Specialist Basic Course (A16T3B4) at the U.S. Marine Corps CBRN School, Ft Leonard Wood, MO. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks refer to reference (ap), Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defense Training and Readiness Manual. See also the 5711 MOS Road Map.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
